take:
Across 5 posts, Qwen is the model creators reach for when they want an agent running on their own hardware. @gigaqian covers Qwen 3.8 27B, which quantizes to about 17 GB at 4-bit and fits on a single RTX 3090 or 4090, and advises using it as the brain of a local agent rather than for chat; the benchmark numbers in the post are Qwen's own, and the creator says to wait for independent evals ([Qwen 3.8 27B](/e/DcCdYgnJ10h)). Unsloth is mentioned as already producing quantized versions.

The hands-on examples run smaller. @cyril.engman carries a rooted OnePlus 8 running Kali NetHunter and a local Qwen model, air-gapped, as an autonomous pen-testing agent he uses to harden his own networks, with every action audit logged ([phone agent](/e/DYNXFvVN0c_)). @codrkai runs an abliterated 9B variant (a version with refusals stripped out) on a 32 GB MacBook Pro through llama.cpp and points an agent harness at it ([local 9B](/e/DeIrl8UJZ0V)). Both appear in [the autonomous agents guide](/guides/autonomous-agents-wild).

An older 2025 post introduces Qwen 2.5 Max as a free model covering chat, code, search, image and video, with the creator claiming it matches ChatGPT ([China's open-source trio](/e/DIaraR1MjLZ)); no other post tests that. DeepSeek co-occurs in 2 posts. One entry, a DIY Claude Code phone remote, tags Qwen without using it ([phone remote](/e/DV84iOPgE5f)). The material here fits people with a 24 to 32 GB machine who want a local agent model, and it is thin on failures or limits beyond hardware size.
